dimensions.assessment: Affects millions of active-duty military personnel, reservists, academy cadets, Department of Defense and Coast Guard civilian employees, and individuals impacted by broad housing, defense, and maritime provisions.
dimensions.evidence: Section 401 authorizes active-duty end strengths for FY2026: Army at 454,000; Navy at 344,600; Marine Corps at 172,300; Air Force at 321,500; and Space Force at 10,400.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes major, life-changing adjustments to military compensation, health care access, service academy rules, and criminal justice/misconduct policies.
dimensions.evidence: Section 705 amends title 10 to cover fertility-related care, including in vitro fertilization, under TRICARE Prime and TRICARE Select for active-duty members and their dependents.

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes massive multi-billion dollar federal funding levels for defense procurement, military construction, energy programs, and allows significant funds transfers.
dimensions.evidence: Section 1001 grants the Secretary of Defense general transfer authority of up to $6,000,000,000 between authorizations for FY2026 upon determining necessity in the national interest.

dimensions.assessment: Amends multiple titles of the U.S. Code, establishes new pilot programs, advisory committees, reporting requirements, and creates wide-ranging regulatory changes for defense, maritime, and housing policy.
dimensions.evidence: The Act is organized into ten divisions covering Department of Defense authorizations, military construction, Department of Energy national security programs, funding tables, additional provisions, intelligence, State Department matters, Coast Guard, housing, and State Department authorizations.

dimensions.assessment: Includes both permanent statutory amendments and multi-year authorizations, pilot programs, and reporting requirements spanning several years or decades.
dimensions.evidence: Section 5247 extends the Puget Sound cetacean desk pilot program from 4 to 6 years.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill is a sweeping omnibus authorization act covering Department of Defense programs, military construction, Department of Energy national security programs, intelligence, Coast Guard policies, housing reforms under the ROAD to Housing Act, and numerous personnel and procurement changes across the military services.

summary: S. 2296, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, sets policies, authorities, and funding levels for Department of Defense programs, military construction, and Department of Energy national security programs. It also incorporates numerous specific acts concerning intelligence activities, coast guard operations, maritime systems, housing reforms, and state department authorizations.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to end strength authorizations, compensation and allowance changes, new training mandates, health care modifications, transition counseling expansions, and conduct regulations.
Impacted by new domestic sourcing restrictions, supply chain illumination requirements, acquisition reform provisions, contracting thresholds, and procurement preferences.
Subject to new authorities, safety requirements, credentialing rules, misconduct tracking systems, and infrastructure oversight under the Coast Guard Authorization Act.

key_provisions: Authorizes fiscal year 2026 appropriations for procurement, research, development, test, evaluation, and operation and maintenance across the military services.
Sets active-duty and reserve end strengths for the military branches for fiscal year 2026.
Places various restrictions, reporting requirements, and inventory floors on aircraft, ships, and weapon programs, including limits on aircraft retirements.

Enacts several specialized measures including the FIGHT China Act, the International Nuclear Energy Act, the AUKUS Improvement Act, the GAIN AI Act, the Intelligence Authorization Act, and the Coast Guard Authorization Act.
Includes major policy updates regarding military health care, personnel management, service academy standards, professional military education, and TRICARE benefits such as fertility care coverage.
Establishes defense acquisition reforms, supply chain security rules, and domestic sourcing mandates to restrict procurements from certain foreign entities of concern.
Reforms housing programs via the ROAD to Housing Act of 2025 and authorizes Department of State operations through the Department of State Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026.
missing_information: Specific dollar amounts for authorized appropriations were not provided in the source text.
Exact numerical totals for military end strengths beyond the listed branch numbers were omitted from the summary notes.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 2296, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026, sets policies, authorities, and funding levels for Department of Defense programs, military construction, and Department of Energy national security programs. It also incorporates numerous specific acts concerning intelligence activities, coast guard operations, maritime systems, housing reforms, and state department authorizations.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation establishes the foundational legal authorities, operational boundaries, and spending policies for the U.S. national defense apparatus and associated agencies for fiscal year 2026, touching nearly every aspect of military procurement, personnel management, and national security strategy.
